item.title: Building China's Social Welfare System During Economic Adjustment
item.description:
Theoretical Horizon (理论前沿), 2009.

Written during the post-2008 adjustment period, this paper discusses how China should build out its social welfare system while the economy is being rebalanced — and why welfare provision and consumption are two sides of the same question.

The full English translation (about 4,500 words) is complete and will be linked here.

item.title: China's Low Consumption Rate and Stage-Based Household Expenditure
item.description:
Lanzhou Academic Journal (兰州学刊), 2010.

This paper examines why China’s household consumption rate stayed low, through the lens of stage-based household expenditure: spending needs arrive in stages across the life cycle, and when several stages bunch together, households compress current consumption. It is the journal version of the flagship paper of my consumption research line; the same study appeared in Contemporary Finance & Economics (当代财经, CSSCI) in 2010.

The full English translation (about 6,000 words, including both tables) is complete and will be linked here.

item.title: Restructuring the Regional Development Model
item.description:
Journal of Hexi University (河西学院学报), 2005.

An early paper on how regional development models in western China needed to be restructured — a theme I returned to in later work on regional equilibrium and agglomeration.

The full English translation (about 4,100 words) is complete and will be linked here.

item.title: The Transformation of Consumption Patterns in China's Marketization Process
item.description:
PhD dissertation, Renmin University of China, 2011. Supervisor: Professor Zhenhua Mao.

This dissertation studies how household consumption in China changed as the economy moved from cash-flow-based consumption — spending constrained by current income — toward a balance-sheet pattern in which assets, credit, and expectations shape spending. It traces the formation of the cash-flow pattern, its persistence in the early reform period, the foundations and paths of the transition, and the risks and obstacles of the balance-sheet pattern, drawing on international experience.
